text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his party aides say that 90 percent of what appeared in the Turkish media about the critical National Security Council meeting is a lie.
- Tansu Ciller, leader of the conservative wing in coalition, threatens to pull out of government if the Islamists do not heed a military warning.
- Two leftist opposition leaders call on Erbakan to resign or recognise the secular status of the state.
- Erbakan says the National Security Council cannot give orders to governments.
- Women march in Istanbul for the continuation of a secular education system.
- A Syrian Christian cemetery in southeastern city of Diyarbakir has been partly demolished by Islamist munipicality in an attempt to widen roads.
- Recent chaos in politics worries the tourism sector.
- Illegal leftist organisations announce demonstrations this month to mark the second anniversary of 20 Alevi Moslems being killed in riots in Gazi district of Istanbul.
